coverage_gaps: The PubMed-only route may miss primary datasets, preprints, patents, trial registries, structural repositories, and full-text details that are absent from abstracts.
Historical discovery terminology and inconsistent indexing may leave early PARK8 or dardarin reports under-retrieved despite synonym expansion.
Rare ancestry-specific variants and penetrance estimates may remain incompletely represented if cohort reports use variant or population names absent from titles and abstracts.
Some proposed LRRK2 substrates may remain unresolved because endogenous validation, tissue relevance, and direct-versus-indirect phosphorylation cannot always be determined from PubMed metadata.
The 12-query limit constrains exhaustive searches for every downstream pathway, animal model, cell type, and contradictory result.
exclusion_criteria: Study mentions LRRK2 or Parkinson disease only incidentally and provides no usable evidence for the question frame.

Claim relies solely on an overexpression or in vitro phosphorylation result without evidence sufficient to label the target physiological; such studies may inform candidate-substrate history but cannot establish physiological substrate status.
Article provides only a narrative assertion when the underlying primary study can be retrieved.
Variant association lacks adequate allele definition, comparator information, or interpretable human-genetic evidence.
Mechanistic experiment lacks a relevant control or cannot separate LRRK2-dependent effects from the stated alternative explanation.
Non-Parkinson disease findings are excluded unless they directly clarify conserved LRRK2 enzymology, substrate biology, or a boundary on Parkinson disease interpretation.
Duplicate records, corrections without substantive evidence, editorials, and non-research commentary are excluded from evidentiary counting.
inclusion_criteria: Publication is indexed in PubMed and has a publication date on or before 2024-12-31.
Study directly addresses LRRK2/PARK8 in Parkinson disease genetics, LRRK2 enzymology, physiological substrate validation, downstream biology, or a limitation of those claims.
Genetic-discovery claims are supported by primary linkage, segregation, mutation-screening, association, or penetrance data; reviews may orient the search but do not replace primary evidence.
Variant claims identify the specific allele and distinguish pathogenic mutations, risk alleles, protective alleles, and variants of uncertain significance when the source permits.
Mechanistic claims report a defined perturbation, biochemical or cellular readout, comparator, and experimental system.

Physiological-substrate claims include endogenous phosphorylation, genetic dependence, pharmacological dependence with a sufficiently selective perturbation, phosphosite evidence, or orthogonal validation in relevant cells or tissues.

Limiting evidence is eligible when it tests penetrance, pathological heterogeneity, variant-specific effects, kinase dependence, substrate specificity, model transferability, or alternative causal explanations.
For duplicated cohorts or overlapping experiments, retain the most complete report while preserving earlier landmark reports needed to trace discovery chronology.

queries.purpose: Locate the foundational linkage, positional-cloning, and independent mutation-discovery reports connecting LRRK2/PARK8 to Parkinson disease.
queries.query: ((LRRK2[Title/Abstract] OR "leucine-rich repeat kinase 2"[Title/Abstract] OR dardarin[Title/Abstract] OR PARK8[Title/Abstract]) AND ("Parkinson Disease"[MeSH Terms] OR Parkinson*[Title/Abstract]) AND (linkage[Title/Abstract] OR cloning[Title/Abstract] OR mutation*[Title/Abstract] OR discovery[Title/Abstract])) AND ("1900/01/01"[Date - Publication] : "2024/12/31"[Date - Publication])

queries.purpose: Identify authoritative syntheses for terminology expansion, landmark-study backtracking, and an initial map of variants, mechanisms, and substrates.
queries.query: ((LRRK2[Title/Abstract] OR PARK8[Title/Abstract]) AND ("Parkinson Disease"[MeSH Terms] OR Parkinson*[Title/Abstract]) AND (review[Publication Type] OR systematic review[Title/Abstract]) AND (genetic*[Title/Abstract] OR kinase[Title/Abstract] OR substrate*[Title/Abstract])) AND ("1900/01/01"[Date - Publication] : "2024/12/31"[Date - Publication])

queries.purpose: Capture late-window studies and reviews that revise variant classification, mechanistic models, substrate validation, biomarkers, or therapeutic implications.
queries.query: ((LRRK2[Title/Abstract] OR "leucine-rich repeat kinase 2"[Title/Abstract]) AND (Parkinson*[Title/Abstract]) AND (variant*[Title/Abstract] OR mechanism*[Title/Abstract] OR substrate*[Title/Abstract] OR Rab[Title/Abstract] OR kinase inhibitor*[Title/Abstract])) AND ("2022/01/01"[Date - Publication] : "2024/12/31"[Date - Publication])

question_frame: Within PubMed-indexed literature published through 2024-12-31, identify and critically connect the genetic discovery of LRRK2 in Parkinson disease, the spectrum and evidentiary status of disease-associated variants, effects of those variants on LRRK2 kinase and ROC-COR GTPase functions, validated physiological substrates and downstream cellular processes, and findings that constrain causal strength, penetrance, substrate specificity, model generalizability, or therapeutic interpretation.
stop_rules: Stop after no new eligible landmark study, variant class, validated substrate class, mechanistic link, or material limitation appears across two consecutive retrieval waves.

Stop a concept branch when at least one primary discovery source and one independent confirmation or qualified contradictory source have been identified, unless the evidence remains materially disputed.
Stop citation backtracking when references repeat already screened records or fall outside the question frame and cutoff.
Stop variant expansion after major established pathogenic mutations and common risk or protective categories are represented and additional alleles do not alter the mechanistic synthesis.
Stop substrate expansion when candidate-only targets are clearly separated from endogenously validated substrates and further records add no new validation modality or biological context.
Stop challenge searching only after penetrance, neuropathological heterogeneity, variant-specific biochemical effects, model dependence, and substrate-causality limitations have each been assessed.
Stop immediately when the 12-query-event budget is exhausted, documenting unresolved branches in coverage_gaps.
Do not infer saturation from review coverage alone; primary-study retrieval and contradiction checks must be completed for each central claim.
